channel.title: Fly Kai Tak blog
channel.description: News and features from Fly Kai Tak, a browser flight simulator of the 1998 Runway 13 approach into Hong Kong Kai Tak.

item.title: New: share your score and report card
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's result screen now has share buttons for X, Facebook, Reddit, WhatsApp, Threads and email, plus a downloadable report card image.

item.title: New: a high score table with Captain and First Officer ranks
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has a high score table. Land the IGS 13 approach by hand to rank as Captain, First Officer, Second Officer, Flight Engineer or Cadet.

item.title: New: giant billboards and neon over Kowloon
item.description: Fly Kai Tak now has 1990s-style giant floodlit billboards on Kowloon rooftops and roadsides, plus glowing neon signs. Brands are invented; no real logos.

item.title: Plane spotter viewpoints: the car park roof and the Peak
item.description: The history of two Kai Tak plane spotting viewpoints, the airport car park roof and the Peak, and how to watch from both in Fly Kai Tak's Plane Spotter mode.

item.title: Update: the rotate prompt is gone
item.description: Fly Kai Tak mobile update: the Turn your phone sideways prompt is removed, so the sim plays in either orientation. Begin descent still asks for landscape full screen.

item.title: Fix: the rotate prompt now clears when you turn your phone
item.description: Fly Kai Tak mobile fix: the rotate prompt now clears when the window turns landscape, with a hint for iPhone players whose Portrait Orientation Lock is on.

item.title: Redrawn aircraft: embedded cockpits and real winglets
item.description: Fly Kai Tak update: the 747-400, 777-200, A330-300 and A340-300 are redrawn with embedded cockpit glass, swept winglets and tapered wings.

item.title: Aircraft now turn smoothly on the ground
item.description: Fly Kai Tak fix: other aircraft snapped to a new heading at every taxi corner. They now curve through turns, ease their speed and line up on the runway.

item.title: The airlines and aircraft of Kai Tak
item.description: A guide to the airlines and aircraft types at Kai Tak in the 1990s: Cathay Pacific, Dragonair, Qantas, BA, Singapore, Thai and JAL, with brief histories.

item.title: Other aircraft now bank the right way
item.description: Fly Kai Tak fix: other aircraft were drawn banking the wrong way in turns. Arrivals and departures now dip the inside wing, as real jets do.

item.title: Read the Fly Kai Tak blog in Cantonese
item.description: The Fly Kai Tak blog now has an English / Cantonese toggle on every page: posts, captions, header and footer switch to written Cantonese.

item.title: Fly Kai Tak in Cantonese: a language toggle on the home screen
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's home screen now has an English / Cantonese toggle: the whole setup screen switches to written Cantonese and remembers your choice.

item.title: The Peak Tram, the Peak Lookout and a view from the Peak
item.description: Fly Kai Tak adds the Peak Tram, the Peak Lookout and a Spectator: The Peak view, alongside Ocean Park's cable car between the Waterfront and the Summit.

item.title: An inverted yoke for touch and mouse: drag down to pull up
item.description: Fly Kai Tak's on-screen yoke is now inverted for touch and mouse: drag down to pull the nose up, drag up to push it down, matching the keyboard.

item.title: Share Fly Kai Tak posts on Threads
item.description: Fly Kai Tak blog posts can now be shared on Threads with one click, with the title and link pre-filled.

item.title: Landmarks tour, plus Ocean Park and Happy Valley
item.description: A tour of the Hong Kong landmarks in Fly Kai Tak, with screenshots, plus the new Ocean Park amusement park and Happy Valley Racecourse.

item.title: Flying Kai Tak on your phone: landscape, a cleaner toolbar and bigger controls
item.description: Fly Kai Tak on mobile: a compact toolbar with a More drawer, landscape touch controls, a rotate prompt for portrait, full screen on Begin descent and safe-area support.

item.title: The checkerboard turn: flying the IGS 13 approach
item.description: How the famous Runway 13 IGS approach into Kai Tak works in Fly Kai Tak: the 088° course, the checkerboard on the hill, the 47° right turn over Kowloon City and the landing grade.

item.title: Real Hong Kong: building 1998 from open data
item.description: How Fly Kai Tak builds Hong Kong from Lands Department open data and SRTM terrain, and the 1998 corrections: no Kai Tak redevelopment, no West Kowloon buildings, and the Walled City as an option.

item.title: Typhoons, fog and city lights: weather and night at Kai Tak
item.description: Weather and night flying in Fly Kai Tak: clear, rain, typhoon, storm, low cloud and fog presets, wind gusts and turbulence, lightning, and a lit-up Kowloon at night.
